newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends down on trade selling, stops hit.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends down on trade selling, stops hit.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled lower weighed down by weather-related trade selling which touched off some sell stops, floor traders said.
Volume was heavy about 15,000 lots changed hands.

The decline was sparked by news of beneficial rains falling over west Texas during the past 24 hours. Rains fell across the west Texas cotton growing region which encompasses about three million acres, Texas A and M cotton specialist Carl Anderson said.
"They were very beneficial for the region especially on the dryland," he said.
"Lamesa, Texas, a major cotton growing area, had 1.34 inches of rain during the last 24 hours," Weather Services Corp meteorologist Mike Palmerino said.
The Delta was also expected to receive beneficial rain in the next 48 hours with moderate temperatures," he said.
But Anderson said the market did not have much direction. "It has been following a narrow channel between 74.50 and 75.50 cents, basis December," he said.
Trade selling led prices downward. "We touched some sell stops at 74.70 cents, basis December and all the way down," a floor source said. Most active December lost 1.00 cent at 74.40 cents a lb.
